facts.text: Standish, Maine, takes its name from Captain Myles Standish of the Plymouth Colony.
Before settlers, the Sokokis tribe of the Abenaki hunted the area Standish, with trails like the Ossipee Trail (now Route 25) and the Pequawket Trail (now Route 113) crossing it.
Saint Joseph's College of Maine, founded in the Mercy tradition, anchors the town’s educational landscape and hosts cultural events and community programs.
Early settlers faced frequent Indian raids that razed cabins and disrupted farming outside protected areas, making frontier life in Standish perilous.
